quick: 0.05 to 0.25 mg once daily (0.1 mg is usual)
summary: Reserpine depletes noradrenaline, dopamine and serotonin from nerve terminals. It is an old, cheap antihypertensive, now rarely used because of depression and other adverse effects; low doses (0.05 to 0.1 mg) with a thiazide are effective.
indications: Hypertension (low dose, usually with a diuretic)

dosage.d: 0.05 to 0.25 mg once daily (0.1 mg is usual)

admin: Use only as the finished product directs
moa: Irreversible VMAT2 inhibition depletes catecholamine and serotonin stores.

absolute: Depression or history of depression, suicidal ideation
Active peptic ulcer or ulcerative colitis

counsel: Use exactly as the pack directs
Stop and seek care for rash, swelling or breathing difficulty
missed: Take it when remembered unless the next dose is due; do not double up.
overdose: No specific antidote. Supportive and symptomatic care.
